newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Ramos calls for more Philippine-Bangladesh trade.
newsitem.headline: Ramos calls for more Philippine-Bangladesh trade.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Thursday that Dhaka and Manila had failed to exploit the economic potential of their friendly ties, and called for a fresh start.

"...1997 marks the 25th year of our diplomatic relations. (But) when we look at the present level of our economic relations, it must be said that we have a lot to catch up on," Ramos told a reception hosted by the Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FBCCI).
Ramos, leading a 120-member delegation that includes top Philippine business figures, arrived in Dhaka on Wednesday on a three-day visit and leaves for Pakistan on Friday.

Trade volume between Dhaka and Manila has been low, with total turnover of just $10 million in 1996. The trade balance favors Dhaka, whose exports to Manila totaled $7.6 million in the year against imports of $2.4 million.
"Just around 0.1 percent of our total exports were sold to Bangladesh...our share of the Bangladesh market is also the lowest vis-a-vis our ASEAN neighbours," Ramos said.

In 1994, Ramos said, Bangladesh bought $474 million worth of goods from Singapore, another member of the ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations), against just $5.4 million from the Philippines.
"I cite all these not to complain, but to show ourselves how much work there is to improve and expand the levels of our relations," he said.

"Our two economies share many things in common. We have a large agriculture sector, a large manpower base. I would emphasize the great importance of seizing the moment to do more business with each other."
The Philippine president urged Bangladeshi entrepreneurs to invest in the southern Philippine island of Mindanao, where a recent peace deal ended a 24-year war with Moslem separatists.
FBCCI President Yusuf Abdullah Harun called for an alliance between ASEAN and the South Asian Assocation of Regional Cooperation (SAARC), of which Bangladesh is a member.
SAARC also groups Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
"I think there is great opportunity for cooperation between the SAARC and the ASEAN countries in terms of production and marketing of each other's products," Ramos told Reuters in a later interview.
"Boundaries are disappearing. Why not think about the whole Asia, a happy cooperative family where stronger members will help weaker ones," Ramos said.

On Wednesday, Ramos and Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina agreed to cooperate on issues ranging from protection of the rights of their workers overseas to the resolution of insurgencies within their borders.
Ramos said he was trying for international consensus on the rights and welfare of migrant workers.
"I have discussed the issue with many countries and will discuss with many more ... the UN convention on the rights of migrant workers and their families must be ratified," he said.
About 3.9 million Filipinos now work in some 130 countries, Ramoes said on Wednesday after a meeting with Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
Hasina said she shared Ramos' concern because Bangladesh had also nearly two million expatriate workers contributing significantly to the country's economy.
Ramos said he was ready to host an international summit on the issue.
